texts.title: Sure you remember it right?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: recall the last appointment you agreed on… which day?
texts.hook.h2.frame: « Sure as I see you »… wrong?
texts.hook.h2: « Sure as I see you »… and still wrong?
texts.hook.h3.frame: Swore Thursday… it became Sunday. How?
texts.hook.h3: I'd have sworn the deadline was Thursday… now I'm sure it's Sunday. How?
texts.hook.h4: An experiment in 10 countries: did people trust their own eyes… or their colleague's words?
texts.hook.h5.frame: Sure of it… who told you?
texts.hook.h5: The date you're sure of… did you see it written? Or did someone tell you?
texts.s1.n1: This is Karim, out of the meeting.
texts.s1.l2: The boss said delivery is on Sunday.
texts.s1.l4: Sunday… the boss said it right in front of me.
texts.s1.a4: And you… if someone told you another day?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time he writes it down as he walks out.
texts.s1.l6: The boss said delivery is on Sunday.
texts.s1.l7: I wrote Thursday… shall we ask him?
texts.book.card: Our memories change easily… so hold your certainty more lightly.
texts.book.l1: The book says: we mix things up easily… so don't believe yourself too much.
texts.book.l2: Like a childhood moment your family told so often… it became your own memory.
texts.verdict.nuance: But your certainty before any talk carries weight, not proof… after talk and time, you can stay sure and be wrong.
texts.verdict.l2: In 10 countries, pairs watched two versions of a film with small differences… after talking, most times they picked their partner's detail.
texts.verdict.l3: And some people were told they got lost as children… so they remembered it, and it never happened.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Karim: write the agreement down as soon as it's said… and go back to it when you disagree. It may help.
texts.share: Send this to someone you argue with about « who said what ».
